title: Why Eiffel’s Lattice Saves the Tower
topic: Why the French engineer Gustave Eiffel built the internal lattice of the Eiffel Tower (to reduce wind resistance and material weight)

lines: Gustave Eiffel hoisted a massive iron beam, then tossed it aside.
Critics shouted, “It looks like a giant grill—useless and ugly!”
Eiffel watches the wind howl over Paris.
He knows the storm could snap a solid tower like a twig.
You see how a bicycle’s frame feels lighter when its tubes are spaced, not solid.
Eiffel designs a lattice of criss‑crossing iron girders.
The open web lets air flow through, cutting pressure on every point.
At the same time the empty spaces shave off tons of weight.
Because of that airy skeleton, the tower sways only nine centimeters in a gale.
The “ugly grill” became the world’s most celebrated wind‑proof monument.

claims.claim: Eiffel’s primary design concern was wind resistance, leading to the lattice structure.
The lattice reduces wind pressure and material weight, allowing the tower to sway only about nine centimeters in strong winds.
Eiffel presented the curved silhouette as a structural principle to handle wind loads efficiently.
